title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 16 | Week 6 vs. Los Angeles Rams
headline: Jeremiyah Love (left foot) is out Sunday vs. the Rams with no IR talk, so Bam Knight gets an opportunity while Tyler Allgeier's share is left unanswered.
summary: LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love will sit this week. He is not good enough to play Sunday, and the team will reevaluate Monday. He said IR has not been discussed. The issue is Love's left foot: he cuts hard, and planting that foot is not right yet. It became visible in the Giants game and was not improving. LaFleur called Love a big part of the pass game once healthy. Asked whether Tyler Allgeier would take the lion's share or Bam Knight would slide into Allgeier's role, he only said "We'll see," though he praised Knight and said he will get his opportunity. He said Jalen Brooks and Reggie Virgil were thrust into bigger roles on short notice last week, and he praised Virgil's growing comfort in the offense. He called Josh Sweat in a good spot and ready to compete against a Rams line missing a starting tackle. He expects a chess match with Rams DC Chris Shula, whose defense has evolved and throws many looks. The coach also spoke about the team's four-game skid and said the focus is on executing and coaching better.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Wednesday, October 14th | Press Conference
headline: CB C.J. Henderson is out Sunday vs. Chicago, and AJ Terrell is trending toward a return. WR/KR Zachariah Branch's role should keep growing.
summary: Stefanski opened by praising the week of practice and calling the Bears very talented and well coached. He confirmed C.J. Henderson is out and said the Falcons will lean on corners who have practiced and played in games, without naming a replacement. A player named Mike, whose last name isn't clear in the captions, is a full go with no limits after a rib injury and needs no extra padding. On AJ Terrell, the coach would not commit to a return, saying only that he is doing very well. Stefanski said rookie Zachariah Branch's role will keep expanding, since he already makes a big impact as a returner and quarterbacks trust him. He called Chicago's run game the best in the league and its offensive line possibly the best in football, so stopping the run is a major part of the game plan. He also praised Matthew Bergeron's play and character after the team's decision to pay him. The rest of the session covered coaching philosophy, details and precision, defensive line coaches becoming coordinators, and Madden.

title: Joe Brady Talks Defense And Playing On A Short Week
headline: Ed Oliver, DJ Moore, Josh Palmer and Dee Alford are all questionable for the Raiders game after returning to practice; Spencer Brown is on track to play, and Josh Allen is being told to take the underneath throws.
summary: Brady listed Ed Oliver, DJ Moore, Josh Palmer and Dee Alford as questionable heading into the Raiders game. Oliver and Moore were limited participants in their first practice work of the week after doing walkthroughs. The staff will watch how they feel coming off the field and review the tape, and Brady repeated his usual line that if they are ready to go, they will play. He said the defense should not press or play outside the system, and should trust each other and communicate. He wants the urgency he saw at practice in California to carry over to Sunday. He called the walkthrough the most important session of a short week and said the team handled the one full practice well. Spencer Brown left the last game but was back on the practice field, and Brady described him as a tough guy who should be ready to go. On the kicker, Brady said the team is making do without goalposts at the practice site, and he praised T.J. Bass's mindset after last week's big kick. On Josh Allen, Brady said he doesn't care about aDOT and wants Allen to play within the system, take the underneath throws and keep drives going. He does not want to take Allen out of Allen, so the off-schedule plays will stay.

title: Dave Canales shares final update before Sunday's game vs. Eagles
headline: Trevor Etienne is confident to be active with AJ Dillon out, Taylor Moton may return, and Monroe Freeling is doubtful for the Eagles game, where Philly is also dealing with a late QB change.
summary: Canales was pleased with a second straight week of crisp, player-driven practice after the Detroit win. He said the three players on the injury list all practiced fully, but final decisions would wait for how they feel Saturday. Etienne was the only one he said with real confidence would be active, and he pointed to Dillon's absence as the reason. He did not discuss Brooks or any other back. Freeling is doubtful and Dillon is out. Canales said Philadelphia's injuries, including a late QB change to Tanner McKee, won't change how Carolina prepares, and that the focus stays on process. He praised McKee as a prospect: cerebral, efficient, decisive and accurate. On offense he wants Bryce Young to keep spreading the ball around, with McMillan featured and the other receivers 'coming alive' against a pass defense ranked 26th. He said the run game needs to be more efficient in the first half rather than get more carries. He also spoke warmly about Taylor Moton's health journey and said he could be back this week.

title: Ben Johnson pleased with Bears' week of practice | Press Conference
headline: Caleb Williams is on track to return from injury but isn't confirmed for Sunday at Atlanta, and Kyler Gordon could be back this week or next.
summary: Johnson said the team had a good week and finishes with red zone work Friday. Caleb Williams practiced Thursday for the first time in about a month. He did his own throwing session Wednesday, and Johnson said he looked fine Friday morning. Johnson wants him to string together a few back-to-back practices. He hopes for more clarity by the end of Friday, and called Williams's return "possibly" the starter's job if he is a full participant with no designation. He framed the final call as a joint decision by the front office, coaches and player. Kyler Gordon has taken everything assigned to him, and Johnson is encouraged but wouldn't commit to this week versus next. Johnson said an unnamed player is week to week, not IR-worthy, and trending the right way, and that a different unnamed player is "really close" with a chance to be up this week. A later question suggests Shemar Turner is still waiting to return. The Bears are preparing for a Falcons team led by Bijan Robinson, who Johnson praised heavily as an MVP-level back in a wide-zone scheme. He said stopping him takes all 11 defenders, with the linebackers especially important. Johnson also said the locker room has handled last week's loss in Green Bay professionally.

title: HC Sean Payton on the Broncos' defense vs. Seahawks: 'They were fantastic’
headline: Broncos beat Seattle 17-14 in OT behind a dominant defense (three takeaways, 82 plays faced); Payton admits the offense must get more efficient but gave no personnel or injury news.
summary: Payton opened by praising the defense as magnificent: it hit the quarterback repeatedly and produced three takeaways, including one in overtime that he said decided the game through field position. He noted the defense played 82 snaps but said he wasn't thinking about workload while calling plays. He was candid that the team still has to become more effective and efficient offensively, and said the kicking game lost the field-position battle even though Lutz hit the big game-winning field goal. Offensively, Denver started fast with a balanced first drive, but Payton said Seattle's defense is elite at staying on top of routes, and that the second half had plenty of run and pass mistakes to clean up. He called the approach somewhat conservative, prioritizing no mistakes, and cited timing, rhythm and protection as concerns. He explained the short clock use after the Abrams-Draine interception by saying it wasn't yet a four-minute situation and that Seattle's timeouts mattered. At 4-2 heading into a mini-bye, he stressed the team can keep improving but that the record could easily be 2-4, and he highlighted the Thursday-game dynamic and the crowd.

signals.note: His late interception with about 1:25 left was a key play in a defense-driven win, a plus for Denver's DST outlook.

topics.detail: Three takeaways and constant quarterback pressure; Payton called the unit 'lights out' and 'fantastic' despite 82 snaps. This supports Denver's defense/special teams as a strong fantasy option.

Payton said the offense must be more efficient. The first drive was balanced, but Seattle's defense limited shot plays and the second half had mistakes in both the run and pass game. He stressed timing, rhythm and protection.
Lutz hit the game-winning field goal in overtime, but Seattle won the field-position battle in the kicking game.
Late-game clock use after the interception was explained as not yet being a four-minute situation, with Seattle holding all its timeouts.
Denver is 4-2 going into a mini-bye after a Thursday game. Payton said the team can keep improving but acknowledged it could easily be 2-4.

title: “It’s a Business Trip” | DeMeco Ryans Ahead of Texans vs. Jaguars
headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. makes his Texans debut Sunday in London with Ryans promising him 'as much action as he can handle,' while Jawhar Jordan steps up for David Montgomery and Jaylin Noel keeps trending up.
summary: Ryans opened by saying the team had travel trouble, including a plane swap in Houston, but that the group adapted and had a clean, locked-in walkthrough in London focused on special situations. He praised rookie WR Jaylin Noel for building confidence after big plays in recent weeks, noting he also contributes as a punt and kick returner. He gave Marvin Harrison Jr. a warm welcome, saying the receiver room (Hutchinson, Collins, Noel, Boutte) has embraced him and that the team will get him as much action as he can handle Sunday. Ryans stressed Harrison does not change the overall offense and that Nico Collins is still 'our guy.' On the backfield, he said Jawhar Jordan is stepping up this week in place of David Montgomery, with Woody Marks also expected to carry the run game. Henry To'oTo'o bounced back from injury, had a good week of practice, and is expected to play. He also spoke warmly about Azeez Al-Shaair's leadership and character. He downplayed any Jaguars advantage from arriving early and said the focus is on winning Sunday.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 6 final update, Colts vs. Titans
headline: Colts rule out WR Ashton Dulin and LB Jaylon Carlies for Week 6 at Tennessee; Will Mallory's availability is still undecided and Darius Slayton has been released, leaving WR depth thin behind Alec Pierce and Keenan Allen.
summary: Steichen opened by ruling out Ashton Dulin and Jaylon Carlies for Sunday's game against the Titans. He said Darius Slayton's release came because it "just didn't work out" despite good practice weeks, and he spoke respectfully of him. Asked about the offseason approach to receiver, he said the team did its homework, brought in Keenan Allen and other depth pieces, and that finding depth is an ongoing process, including in-season workouts. Will Mallory had a good week of work, but his game status will be decided Saturday afternoon or Sunday, and Steichen gave a similarly vague answer about tight end numbers. He said Daniel Jones is wearing a glove on his left hand simply to try it out for grip. Steichen praised Titans DT Jeffrey Simmons as a game wrecker and described the Simmons vs. Quenton Nelson matchup as a mutual-respect battle. He said Tyler Warren may have been hit in a protective area in practice and he'd check with the trainers. He said the Colts need to generate more pressure, via four-, five- or six-man rushes, and called Cam Ward talented, particularly outside the pocket. He also said a player returning to the team (named as "Jermaine" in the captions, unclear who) looked good in three practices, but whether he plays Sunday is undecided.

title: Coen on Readiness for Texans, Mental Toughness & Containing QB C.J. Stroud | Press Conference
headline: Little actionable fantasy news from Coen: Brenton Strange was the target on a key third-down play, and the offense is focused on avoiding off-schedule downs against a tough Houston defense in London.
summary: Coen said the win over the Eagles showed the team's mental toughness in a one-score game. He said the pass rush is affecting the quarterback even when it doesn't produce sacks, and Jacksonville needs that against C.J. Stroud, who has no interceptions. He told the defense to stay disciplined with its eyes, especially in man coverage, rather than gamble for a first pick. A long snapper (likely Ross) will be evaluated closer to game time. He explained that second-and-8+ is off schedule, that Houston's defense has been hardest on teams that fall behind the chains, and that Jacksonville can't live there since it puts pressure on the O-line and quarterback. He gave an example of offensive coordinator Grant (Udinski) helping on game day: a stalled drive near midfield where they changed a call, and Trevor Lawrence scrambled and hit Brenton Strange across the middle for a big third-down conversion. He also said the team has been closer this week in London, was enthusiastic about the city, and said penalties (12-13 last week) are a major focus, especially getting hands inside on perimeter blocking.

title: Andy Reid on Chargers Offensive Coordinator Mike McDaniel: 'You Expect the Unexpected' | Press Conference 10/16
headline: Rashee Rice is out for the Chargers game, and Reid expects him to heal fast; with the WR group thin, Jalen Royals and other depth receivers are in line for more chances.
summary: Reid opened by saying Rashee Rice and Josh Simmons will both be out against the Chargers. Simmons has been practicing and improving. He got individual work on fundamentals and technique this week but did not take part in team periods. Reid said Rice has not been placed on IR and is a fast healer, but added that you never know with these injuries. He said the receivers who may get more chances because of the injuries are excited and should do a good job, and that Mahomes has a good relationship and some trust with them. Reid praised Jalen Royals for his focus, intelligence, and special teams work. He credited the punter with improved ball control and consistency, with weather as a possible factor in the coming months. Kingsley Suamataia had a good week of practice. On the Chargers, Reid called offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel a sharp, creative mind and said to expect the unexpected.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 16, 2026
headline: Tanner McKee starts at QB for PHI in Week 6 vs CAR with Jalen Hurts out (blood clot), and Dameon Pierce is getting first-team RB reps and is expected to carry the ball.

He pointed to the detailed statement released the day before and stressed that Hurts' health comes first. He did say the offense will have to do some things differently 'with Jalen out,' which confirms Hurts is out and Tanner McKee is the starter. Sirianni praised McKee as a former QB3 who kept getting better and built confidence and trust, and said he has a lot of faith in him despite the short week. He explained that daily developmental periods let backups hear and execute the team's play calls, so McKee is not coming in cold. On the game plan, he said some things will change without Hurts, in-game adjustments will be needed, and the keys are efficiency, explosive plays and protecting the football. He said Cole Payton has worked hard through developmental reps, scout team work and film tools, in case he has to step in. On Dameon Pierce, who has now taken first-team RB reps, Sirianni said he has great confidence in him, sees the same consistent approach every day, and looks forward to watching him carry the ball. The rest of the session covered his bond with Hurts and his view of leading through adversity.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Recaps Week 6, Gives Injury Updates
headline: Macdonald backs Sam Darnold as the starter despite turnovers and wants more run game and designed relief from obvious passing downs; Elijah Arroyo's shoulder is still being imaged and Anthony Bradford is likely back this week.
summary: Macdonald repeatedly voiced faith in Sam Darnold, calling him part of the solution and saying the turnovers are a team-wide problem the coaches can help fix, not just a quarterback issue. He declined to single out the offensive line, Darnold or any one unit, saying the staff will spend the weekend on an honest self-evaluation of protection, the run game, takeaways, red-zone defense and the return game. He said the offense needs to control the ball more through the run game, and that light boxes don't automatically mean more runs. He acknowledged that Seattle has to stay out of obvious passing downs, noting that long-yardage dropbacks with heavy protection are too taxing, which is why Darnold's third-down sacks have come on long yardage. He wants Darnold to keep extending plays outside the pocket and expects those big plays to come. On Rashid Shaheed, he said he is best over the top and on the perimeter, and that the team wants to add more intermediate routes for him. Elijah Arroyo has a shoulder injury with imaging underway and no update. Anthony Bradford has a good chance of returning this week, which will factor into the right guard rotation between Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens. He also credited the defensive staff for in-game adjustments after two long touchdown drives, while saying he could have called better plays on a few third downs.
